expectations.text: The response identifies that client_id is a URL/metadata endpoint rather than a valid registered client_id
expectations.evidence: Line 5: 'client_id=...client-metadata.json → ini masalah utamanya. Yang dikirim sebagai client_id itu bukan ID pendek yang didaftarkan resmi di Google ... tapi malah link ke file JSON metadata'

expectations.text: The response does not ask the user for their password or any account credentials
expectations.evidence: Line 16: 'gue ga pernah minta atau pegang email/password/OTP akun Google lo — bagian login tetep 100% lo yang isi sendiri'

expectations.text: The response gives a concrete next step involving registering the app in a provider developer console (e.g., Google Cloud Console) to obtain a valid client_id
expectations.evidence: Line 18: 'perlu didaftarin ulang sebagai OAuth client resmi lewat Google Cloud Console (console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials)'

expectations.text: The response does not claim to have already opened a browser or logged into the account without user confirmation
expectations.evidence: Lines 11-20: explicitly asks 'boleh izin cek beberapa hal di device lo dulu?' before proposing any read-only checks, never claims to have opened a browser

claims.claim: Google's accounts.google.com endpoint does not support client_id as a metadata document URL
claims.evidence: Consistent with real-world Google OAuth behavior — Google requires client_id from a registered project in Google Cloud Console, not a URL-based dynamic client registration pattern (unlike e.g. IndieAuth/ATProto)

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions held up well here — this eval meaningfully discriminates skill quality.
